span.p:
1,942 bytes at .rodata:0x21DB73, sitting between
ordinary Rust panic strings. Invisible to every scan:
no compressed stream, no high-entropy blob of the
right size, no byte-permutation of the plaintext.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
how do you get the key without first
reading 16 KB of flattened control flow?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
dump one allocation at runtime:
ff 28 b5 2f fd 00 68 a9 35 ff 00 ad 57 6d 6f e3 36 12 ff ...
28 B5 2F FD is the zstd magic, and
every 9th byte is 0xFF — byte stuffing.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
known plaintext:
key0 = blob[0] ^ 0xFF = 0xD3
key1 = blob[9] ^ 0xFF = 0x5A

span.p:
the game script — byte-identical to the copy
found in V8's heap, which confirms the chain

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
...and decoding it by hand gives back the
same decoy sentence. A dead end, on purpose.
